title: Lior and the Orchard
premise: Coral Ashgrove's café is three missed payments from collapse when her mother demands she attend the Ashgrove family reunion with proof she's 'settled.' Desperate, she hires Lior Vane, a quiet orchard caretaker with his own buried past, to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. What begins as a transaction turns tender through shared recipes, orchard walks, and the slow discovery that Lior is the estranged heir of the development company threatening to buy out her street—including her café. When the truth surfaces, Coral must choose between the family loyalty she's always obeyed and the truth of who she loves, while Lior must forgive the man he was before he can claim the man he's becoming. In the end, Lior publicly rejects his inheritance, Coral saves the café by turning it into a community bakery-orchard co-op, and the two plant a new tree where the lie first began.
about_author: Marguerite Fairweather is the pen name of a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, orchards, and small towns on the edge of change. She lives in a converted cider house with her partner and an opinionated lemon tree.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A red-letter notice arrives at Ashgrove Café the same morning her mother calls about the family reunion. Coral burns a batch of her signature tarts, a rare failure that mirrors her life. Emotional beat: quiet desperation masked with dry humor.

chapters.title: The Reunion Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Her mother insists Coral bring a partner to the Ashgrove centennial reunion or endure a weekend of pity. Coral's sister Dahlia offers to set her up with a dentist; Coral would rather eat her own whisk. Emotional beat: stubborn pride hardening into a bad decision.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fixed the Awning
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A stranger quietly repairs her storm-torn awning at dawn and refuses payment, asking only for coffee and a seat. He's Lior, new caretaker at the old Fairweather orchard on the edge of town. Emotional beat: first flicker of curiosity.

chapters.title: An Indecent Proposal, Pastry-Flavored
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, half-drunk on exhaustion and elderflower cordial, Coral offers Lior money to be her fake boyfriend. He laughs, then surprises her by saying yes—for a price she can't yet afford, payable after the reunion. Emotional beat: reckless hope.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior agrees to the arrangement, telling himself it's cover for his own secret errand in town. We glimpse his locked satchel of documents and his rule: never get known, never get caught. Emotional beat: controlled man making an uncontrolled choice.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner for Two
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Fake-couple practice in the empty café—how they met, first date, pet names—turns uncomfortably easy. Lior tastes her failed tart and tells her exactly what's missing. Emotional beat: intimacy arriving through craft.

chapters.title: Arrival at Ashgrove House
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The reunion begins: aunts, rivals, her mother's appraising eyes. Lior plays his role flawlessly, charming even Great-Aunt Winifred. Coral realizes she didn't brief him well enough for him to be this good. Emotional beat: suspicion blooming under gratitude.

chapters.title: The Orchard Walk
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior walks the reunion grounds and recognizes the heritage apple rows—trees his family catalogued decades ago. A cousin of Coral's mentions the development company sniffing around the street. Lior's stomach drops. Emotional beat: guilt taking root.

chapters.title: Dessert and a Confession She Doesn't Hear
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral wins the reunion bake-off with a recipe Lior helped rescue; her mother almost smiles. Lior starts to tell her something, then Winifred interrupts. Emotional beat: the almost-told truth.

chapters.title: One Bed, Two Liars
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The inn double-books; Coral and Lior share a room, talking until 3 a.m. about failure, family, and second chances. Neither lies outright; neither tells everything. Emotional beat: the fake becoming real by lamplight.

chapters.title: Sunday Goodbyes
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The reunion ends warmly—too warmly. Coral's mother invites 'Lior' to Sunday dinners, and Coral can't bring herself to end the arrangement. Emotional beat: the con outliving its purpose.

chapters.title: The Satchel
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Alone, Lior reviews the documents: he is the estranged son of Edmund Vane, founder of Vane Development, the company buying Coral's street. He came to assess, not to fall. Emotional beat: self-loathing sharpening.

chapters.title: Flour and Forgiveness
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Back home, business worsens. Lior starts showing up daily, working the counter, fixing equipment, becoming part of the café's rhythm. Regulars adopt him. Emotional beat: belonging he never planned to keep.

chapters.title: The Eviction Letter
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Vane Development delivers formal buyout notices to the whole block. Coral's landlord has already signed intent. The café's deadline: ninety days. Emotional beat: dread with a deadline.

chapters.title: An Expert on the Enemy
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The café crew plots resistance, and Lior—knowing exactly how Vane operates—gives chillingly accurate advice. Coral notices he never says 'they' like an outsider. Emotional beat: the noose of knowledge tightening.

chapters.title: First Real Date
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral asks Lior on a real date, no pretense. Cider house, slow dancing, a kiss under the orchard's oldest tree. Lior nearly confesses; instead he kisses her again. Emotional beat: happiness built on a fault line.

chapters.title: Edmund Vane's Son
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior visits his father's office to delay the buyout from the inside. Edmund offers him the CEO seat if he closes the Ashgrove Street acquisition personally. Emotional beat: the past demanding a price.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Recognized Him
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Mr. Okafor from the hardware store shows Coral an old photo: a teenage boy beside Edmund Vane. It's Lior. Coral says nothing, testing, watching. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth beginning their war.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Knows
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior reveals to Coral that Vane is his father—omitting that he's here on assignment. He frames himself as a runaway heir who hates the company. It's mostly true. Coral chooses to believe him. Emotional beat: mercy granted on incomplete truth.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Sixty Left
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The café community rallies: petitions, a save-the-café bake sale, local press. Coral's mother disapproves of the 'circus.' Coral, for once, stops seeking her approval. Emotional beat: Coral finding her spine.

chapters.title: The Offer He Can't Refuse
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Edmund escalates: sign the acquisition or Lior's name—and his past misdeeds that drove him from the company—go public to Coral and the town. Emotional beat: blackmail closing like a fist.

chapters.title: The Bake Sale Sabotage
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Someone reports the bake sale for unlicensed vending; inspectors shut it down. A Vane signature move. Coral watches Lior's face and sees recognition, not surprise. Emotional beat: trust cracking.

chapters.title: Confession at the Counter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lior admits everything: his name, his mission, the satchel, the deal he refused and the one he's being blackmailed over. Coral, shattered, asks the only question that matters: 'Was any of it real?' He can't answer fast enough. Emotional beat: heartbreak in real time.

chapters.title: Empty Chairs
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral throws him out. The café feels cavernous without him; her hands keep making his favorite tart out of habit, then she throws that away too. Emotional beat: grief that tastes like flour.

chapters.title: The Mirror
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Alone in the orchard cottage, Lior confronts the man in the mirror—the son who ran, the liar who stayed, the man who loved and still chose the safe silence. He decides the inheritance he wants isn't Edmund's. Emotional beat: the forgiveness of self begins.

chapters.title: Dahlia's Discovery
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Sister Dahlia uncovers that Lior has been secretly funding the block's legal defense through a shell nonprofit—and that his testimony could void the buyout on zoning fraud. Coral learns he was fighting for her even after she banished him. Emotional beat: hope arriving sideways.

chapters.title: Mother's War
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral's mother forbids her from the hearing, invoking family loyalty: 'Vanes ruin Ashgroves.' Coral finally names the family pattern—duty dressed as love—and walks out of Ashgrove House for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: the break that is a birth.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At the zoning hearing, Lior testifies to Vane's forged signatures, sacrificing his name, his father, and any future in the company. Edmund disowns him publicly. Emotional beat: burning the bridge behind him.

chapters.title: The Question in the Hallway
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral arrives too late for the testimony but finds Lior in the hallway, hollowed out. She asks if he's forgiven himself. He says he's trying. She says trying is the only recipe she trusts. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered, not yet accepted.

chapters.title: Edmund's Last Card
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Edmund threatens to demolish the orchard itself—the trees Lior restored—out of spite. Lior realizes the orchard, not the company, is his true inheritance. Emotional beat: clarity through loss.

chapters.title: The Town Stands Up
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The hearing's final day: the whole street shows, bake sale receipts, Okafor's ledger, Dahlia's research. The buyout is voided. The street cheers; Coral looks for one face. Emotional beat: collective victory, private ache.

chapters.title: What He Couldn't Say
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior writes Coral a letter he doesn't send, then decides some things must be said standing up, in flour-dusted light. Emotional beat: courage assembling itself.

chapters.title: The Oldest Tree
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Lior comes to the café, not with excuses but with the deed option he secured: the orchard's oldest tree row, offered to the neighborhood in perpetuity. Then, in front of everyone, he tells Coral he loves her and that she owes him nothing. Emotional beat: love without leverage.

chapters.title: Her Answer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral doesn't answer with words. She hands him the tart she'd thrown away the recipe to remake—the one he fixed—and says, 'Stay for dessert. Stay for all of it.' Emotional beat: the yes.

chapters.title: Mother, Thawing
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral's mother appears at the café, stiff, and orders 'whatever he always has.' It's the closest thing to an apology the Ashgroves produce. Coral accepts it as such. Emotional beat: reconciliation in the family dialect.

chapters.title: The Co-op Plan
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Coral and Lior draft the plan: Ashgrove Café becomes a community bakery-orchard co-op, the block collectively holds the lease, Lior manages the trees. The café's debt dissolves into shared ownership. Emotional beat: survival turned into something better.

chapters.title: Edmund at the Gate
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Edmund comes to the orchard one last time, expecting a fight. Lior offers him an apple from the tree his grandfather planted. Edmund can't take it, but he can't leave either. Emotional beat: the door left unlocked.

chapters.title: Harvest Day
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. First community harvest: the whole street in the orchard, tarts made from fruit picked that morning, Lior's flour-dusted hands in hers. Coral's mother laughs at something Dahlia says. Emotional beat: abundance earned.

chapters.title: Planting the New Tree
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the anniversary of the fake date, Coral and Lior plant a sapling where they first kissed, burying the old buyout contract beneath the roots as fertilizer. 'Second chances,' Coral says, 'are for people with better timing.' 'Or people who make the time,' he answers. Emotional beat: the promise made permanent.

chapters.title: Lior and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue voice. A year later: the café thrives, the co-op holds, and Coral renames the menu's signature tart 'The Lior'—bitter edge, sweet finish. Final image: the two of them under the oldest tree as blossom falls like the first snow of a better year. Emotional beat: home, at last, in every sense.
